title: Baked oats with rhubarb and orange

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, sugar, oil, fresh fruit, walnuts and spices are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Tesco stocks forced rhubarb in January, and everything else is an everyday item.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a baking dish, a bowl and a grater, and the method is mix and bake.

works.reason: 200g oats to about 500ml of water and juice, baked for 35 minutes at 190°C, gives a set bake for four; the rhubarb will soften on top, though it may be a little sharp.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is enough to grate two apples, zest and juice the oranges, chop the rhubarb and mix, and the 35-minute bake matches the step.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, names match their ids, and only water is added.

seasonal_feel.reason: January citrus and early forced rhubarb suit a warm winter breakfast, and orange is in the base through zest and juice and is served alongside.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British-English instructions with no fuss or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling oat bake with plenty of fruit, nuts and only a little sugar, the sort of breakfast a family would make again.
